bc_capone_wall.blurb: Capone Wall is a small sport crag in the Rogues Gallery zone of Cheakamus Canyon, on the road between Squamish and Whistler. It holds ten bolted lines, with a pair of top-rope-friendly options among them. The grade spread leans hard: one climb in the 5.10 range, a cluster in the low to mid 5.11s, a few 5.12s and a couple of 5.13s, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper, technical faces rather than beginners. The wall looks toward the south and west, and the canyon sits a little inland, which tends to leave it drier than the coastal crags near town. Expect a short tour of a single wall rather than a full day of mileage.

bc_andre_s_wall.blurb: Andre's Wall is a bolted face in the Chek zone of Cheakamus Canyon, in the Sea to Sky corridor north of Squamish. Ten sport routes are recorded, with a couple of two-pitch outings among the single pitches. Difficulty is centred on the 5.10s, with a few 5.11s, one 5.12 and a couple of easier warm-ups near 5.7 and 5.8, so it works for intermediates who want a mid-grade tick list close to the campground. The routes carry a range of climbing styles rather than one repeating move. Plan on a quick stop for a handful of lines, or pair it with the neighbouring walls at Chek.
bc_andre_s_wall.approach: A short stroll from the middle campground at Chek; heading toward Ursa Minor, the wall is reached at a bench beside the trail.

bc_mother_earth.blurb: Mother Earth is a cluster of ten boulder problems within the Grohman Narrows bouldering zone, in the West Kootenay region of British Columbia near Nelson. The blocks are on the tall side and reward technical face climbing, cracks and corners rather than pure power moves, which sets them apart from much of the rest of the area. Most problems fall between V1 and V3, with a handful around V5 and a single harder test near V6, so there is something for a mixed group. A short session here pairs easily with other boulders nearby.
